summary: Reviewed the change set for security, resource limits and data integrity; found two high and two medium defects.

findings.summary: Project-controlled .factory symlink redirects init writes outside the repository
findings.evidence: ENG-25 and ENG-26: init accepts an existing symlinked .factory directory through mkdir(exist_ok=True), creates temporary files there and publishes them with os.replace at lines 114-119. A checked-out repository can make .factory point to an external directory lacking config.json; running init creates config.json there and replaces any existing config.README.md there. A temporary-directory reproduction confirmed both effects. The write destination is constrained to those two names, but an unrelated external README can be destroyed.
findings.fix: Reject a symlinked .factory directory and use directory-relative, no-follow operations that prevent a concurrent directory swap from redirecting publication outside the repository.

findings.summary: Unbounded project config reads permit preflight hangs and memory exhaustion
findings.evidence: ENG-24 and ENG-25: resolve reads repository-controlled .factory/config.json using path.read_text() without a file-type check, byte limit or timeout. A symlink to /dev/zero supplies an endless stream and can exhaust process memory; a FIFO with no writer blocks on open. A temporary FIFO reproduction remained blocked until the subprocess timeout. The normal models command and every preflight resolve the project file.
findings.fix: Open the project config without following symlinks, verify that the opened descriptor is a regular file, and read at most a documented small maximum plus one byte, rejecting oversized or special files without blocking.

findings.summary: Concurrent creation between init's existence check and publication is overwritten
findings.evidence: ENG-26 and FR-014: lines 90-91 check config existence before resolving and staging, but os.replace at line 119 overwrites a config created in the intervening window. A reproduction that created config.json immediately before replace confirmed its contents were lost. Concurrent init calls or a user saving config can trigger the race.
findings.fix: Publish the staged config using an atomic no-replace operation or an exclusive creation protocol, refuse if another writer won, and preserve the other writer's bytes.

findings.summary: Untrusted model strings are emitted as raw terminal control sequences
findings.evidence: ENG-25: validation at lines 35-43 accepts any string and report interpolates it verbatim into the human-readable table. A project JSON value containing an escaped OSC 52 sequence was reproduced as raw ESC bytes in factory models output. When displayed by a supporting terminal, repository-controlled output can alter terminal state or clipboard; init also embeds unescaped user values in its printed table and README.
findings.fix: Escape control characters in human-readable table and README output, including ESC and C0/C1 controls, while preserving exact model values in JSON and internal resolution.
